theme: Modern Indus geographic atlas, architectural models and regional continuity evidence
question: Can existing Indus maps support a modern source-linked geographic explorer, detailed architectural models, and separate reviews of changing markers and towns inhabited today?
outcome: The local atlas preserves 115 place entities and 112 located points, exposes source and date quality, imports later coordinate assertions and maps sixteen town or named-place candidates from an eighteen-case review. A separate offline explorer provides seven 3D scenes and top-down plans with metric exports and feature-level assumptions. The continuity study records twelve sources and sixteen observations of regional persistence, changed markers and detectability. No new inscribed object, site discovery, inscription date or continuous Indus-to-present town sequence is claimed.
challenge: Earlier location and chronology records have unequal source quality. Source plans lack common surveyed control, reconstructions need explicit height and placement assumptions, and an early occupation date does not establish uninterrupted habitation. A living-town numeric date correction arrived after the first integration snapshot.
remedy: Retain original coordinates and phases, preserve competing assertions and unlocated labels, separate modern anchors from ancient features, distinguish modelling parameters, and preserve the first map snapshot before building a corrected successor. Link every historical claim to its source review and prospective deciding evidence.
retry_when: Add licensed georeferenced excavation plans, surveyed feature coordinates and architectural-phase joins, new independently dated occupation contexts beneath modern towns, or recovery-controlled ordinary-activity and marker records. Additional generic cultural similarities or reseeding exposed inscriptions do not establish fresh continuity evidence.

authors.agent: map and integration contributor; three parallel contributors have separate attempt records
